construct: time-bounded topic discourse; editorial selection of sub-events is part of coverage

monetary_policy.label: Monetary policy and central banks
monetary_policy.definition: Central-bank decisions, guidance, balance sheets, policy rates, and interpretation of monetary-policy stance.
examples: Federal Reserve signals a slower path for rate cuts
Powell discusses inflation and the policy outlook

inflation_prices.label: Inflation and prices
inflation_prices.definition: Changes in consumer or producer prices, inflation expectations, and economy-wide cost-of-living pressure.
examples: US inflation slows more than economists expected
Consumer prices rise as housing costs remain elevated

labor_markets.label: Labor markets
labor_markets.definition: Employment, unemployment, wages, hiring, layoffs, labor participation, strikes, and economy-wide worker conditions.
examples: Payroll growth slows while unemployment holds steady
Technology companies announce another round of layoffs

growth_recession.label: Growth, demand, and recession
growth_recession.definition: Macroeconomic growth, recession risk, aggregate demand, production, consumption, and broad business-cycle conditions.
examples: Retail sales point to weakening consumer demand
Economy avoids recession as quarterly GDP expands

fiscal_tax_debt.label: Fiscal policy, tax, and sovereign debt
fiscal_tax_debt.definition: Government budgets, taxation, public spending, deficits, sovereign borrowing, and debt-limit disputes.
examples: Debt ceiling negotiations approach their deadline
Government budget combines tax increases with spending cuts

banking_credit.label: Banking, credit, and financial stability
banking_credit.definition: Bank health, bank failures, lending conditions, credit stress, liquidity, and systemic financial stability.
examples: Regional bank deposit flight raises financial-stability concerns
Lenders tighten credit standards after bank failures

corporate_earnings_deals.label: Corporate earnings and deals
corporate_earnings_deals.definition: Firm-level earnings, revenue, guidance, mergers, acquisitions, public offerings, and major corporate restructuring.
examples: Company cuts guidance after quarterly profit misses estimates
Regulators approve the proposed acquisition

market_performance.label: Financial-market performance
market_performance.definition: Observed movements, valuation, liquidity, or positioning in broad equity, bond, currency, volatility, or digital-asset markets.
examples: Wall Street falls as Treasury yields climb
S&P 500 reaches a new high after a broad rally

energy_oil_gas.label: Energy, oil, and gas
energy_oil_gas.definition: Oil and gas production, supply, prices, OPEC policy, energy security, and economically material energy-market disruption.
examples: OPEC agrees to extend oil production cuts
European natural-gas prices rise after a supply disruption

technology_ai_chips.label: Technology, AI, and semiconductors
technology_ai_chips.definition: Artificial intelligence, semiconductors, platform technology, cybersecurity, and economically material technology regulation.
examples: Chipmakers face new export restrictions
Governments negotiate rules for generative artificial intelligence

trade_tariffs.label: Trade, tariffs, and supply chains
trade_tariffs.definition: International trade restrictions, tariffs, export controls, sanctions used primarily as economic policy, and supply-chain restructuring.
examples: United States announces new tariffs on Chinese imports
Manufacturers move supply chains in response to export controls

covid_pandemic.label: COVID-19 pandemic
covid_pandemic.definition: COVID infections, restrictions, vaccines, treatments, public-health policy, and social or economic consequences of the pandemic.
examples: COVID restrictions return as infections increase
Regulator authorizes a new coronavirus vaccine

russia_ukraine.label: Russia-Ukraine war
russia_ukraine.definition: The Russia-Ukraine conflict and its military, political, humanitarian, sanctions, energy, and security consequences.
examples: Ukraine reports a new Russian missile attack
European governments debate further support for Kyiv

israel_gaza.label: Israel-Gaza conflict
israel_gaza.definition: The Israel-Gaza war, Hamas, hostages, ceasefire negotiations, humanitarian conditions, and associated political consequences.
examples: Ceasefire talks continue as fighting persists in Gaza
Families call for the release of Israeli hostages

iran_israel.label: Iran-Israel confrontation
iran_israel.definition: Direct or proxy confrontation between Iran and Israel, including strikes, retaliation, nuclear tensions, and escalation risk.
examples: Iran launches missiles at Israel after an earlier strike
Israel considers its response to Iran's attack

red_sea_houthi.label: Red Sea and Houthi conflict
red_sea_houthi.definition: Houthi attacks, military responses, and disruption to Red Sea or Bab el-Mandeb shipping and trade routes.
examples: Houthi attacks divert shipping away from the Red Sea
US and UK conduct strikes in Yemen after attacks on vessels

us_china_relations.label: U.S.-China relations
us_china_relations.definition: Strategic, diplomatic, military, and economic competition between the United States and China, excluding purely domestic stories.
examples: United States and China resume high-level trade talks
Tensions rise over military activity near Taiwan

climate_transition.label: Climate policy and energy transition
climate_transition.definition: Climate policy, carbon regulation, clean-energy transition, and economically material climate-related disruption.
examples: Government delays parts of its net-zero policy
Clean-energy investment rises under new climate incentives
